source_text:
Θαυμαστὴ μὲν οὖν ἡ
ἐλεημοσύνη, ἀλλὰ χωρὶς πίστεως ἁμαρτημάτων οὐκ ἐργάζεται λύτρωσιν·
«Ἐλεημοσύναις γὰρ καὶ πίστεσιν ἀποκαθαίρονται ἁμαρτίαι.» Ζηλωτὸν ἡ πραότης,
ἀλλὰ χωρὶς τῆς ταπεινώσεως βασιλικὸν ἀποτελέσαι χαρακτῆρα οὐ δύναται·
«Μάθετε γὰρ ἀπ' ἐμοῦ, φησίν, ὅτι πραΰς εἰμι καὶ ταπεινὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ.» Καλὸν ἡ πίστις
ὡς καὶ τὸ βραχύτατον αὐτῆς ὄρη δύνασθαι μεθιστᾶν, ἀλλὰ χωρὶς ἀγάπης εἰκαία καὶ
περιττὴ καθέστηκεν· «Κἂν ἔχω γὰρ πίστιν», φησίν, «ὥστε ὄρη μεθιστάναι, ἀγάπην δὲ
μὴ ἔχω, οὐθέν εἰμι.»
orientation: The preacher continues his chain of paired virtues, now showing that almsgiving needs faith, gentleness needs humility, and faith needs love.
pass_a_gloss: Wonderful then is almsgiving, but without faith it does not work redemption of sins; "For by almsgiving and faith sins are cleansed." Zealous is gentleness, but without humility it cannot produce a royal character; "For learn from me," he says, "that I am gentle and humble in heart." Good is faith, as even the smallest part of it can move mountains, but without love it is vain and superfluous; "For if I have faith," he says, "so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing."

choices.english: does not work redemption of sins
choices.why: Keeps the active force of ἐργάζεται (works/accomplishes) and the objective genitive ἁμαρτημάτων with λύτρωσιν, preserving the literal sense that almsgiving by itself cannot accomplish the release from sins.
rejected: does not bring about forgiveness of sins

choices.term: Ἐλεημοσύναις γὰρ καὶ πίστεσιν ἀποκαθαίρονται ἁμαρτίαι
choices.english: For by almsgivings and faiths sins are cleansed
choices.why: Renders the plural nouns literally (almsgivings, faiths) and keeps the passive ἀποκαθαίρονται as 'are cleansed,' matching the source's plural instrumentals.
rejected: For sins are cleansed by almsgiving and faith
For alms and faith purge away sins

choices.why: Keeps βασιλικόν as 'royal' and χαρακτήρα as 'character,' with ἀποτελέσαι as 'produce/accomplish,' preserving the metaphor of forming a kingly stamp or mark.
Renders both adjectives literally (εἰκαία = vain/empty, περιττή = superfluous/excessive) and keeps καθέστηκεν as 'it stands/is established,' preserving the perfect sense.
rejected: it amounts to nothing and is excessive

choices.why: Keeps the infinitive μεθιστάναι as 'to move' with ὥστε expressing result/purpose, matching the literal force of the conditional quotation.

bible_refs.note: Μάθετε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ ὅτι πραΰς εἰμι καὶ ταπεινὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ
Κἂν ἔχω πίστιν ὥστε ὄρη μεθιστάναι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐθέν εἰμι

pass_b_english: Almsgiving, then, is wonderful, but without faith it does not work redemption from sins. For he says, "By almsgiving and faith sins are cleansed." Gentleness is something to be zealous for, but without humility it cannot produce a royal character. For the Lord says, "Learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart" (Matthew 11:29). Faith is good, since even the smallest measure of it can move mountains, but without love it is vain and superfluous. For he says, "Even if I have faith so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing" (1 Corinthians 13:2).

problems.source_quote: Ἐλεημοσύναις γὰρ καὶ πίστεσιν ἀποκαθαίρονται ἁμαρτίαι
problems.why: The quote matches Tobit 12:9, not Proverbs 15:27.
The source quotes Sirach 3:30 (LXX), not Tobit 12:9. The wording matches Sirach.
problems.ruling: Source Ἐλεημοσύναις...ἀποκαθαίρονται ἁμαρτίαι matches Sirach 3:30 LXX, not Tobit 12:9; wrong reference misleads reader.

fixed: Changed the scripture citation from Tobit 12:9 to Sirach 3:30, matching the source wording.

Plural 'faiths' appears only in Sirach quote, unlike singular elsewhere.

problems.fix: Identify speaker as 'the Lord' for Gospel citations.

problems.why: Same concept rendered singular and plural in same sentence, confusing readers.
problems.fix: Use 'faith' consistently; the plural is a literal gloss.

fixed: Changed 'almsgivings and faiths' to 'almsgiving and faith' in the Sirach quote to standardize singular forms.
Identified the speaker as 'the Lord' for the Matthew 11:29 citation.
The 1 Corinthians 13:2 citation remains 'he says' because the source uses φησίν without naming the speaker; the English already matches the source.
Removed the incorrect Sirach 3:30 reference; the quote is not from Sirach 3:30, so the citation was removed rather than replaced with a wrong reference.

last_rejected.why: The source quotes Sirach/Ecclesiasticus, but the work brief states only Gospels and Pauline epistles are cited in this fragment; Psalms are not cited. Sirach is deuterocanonical and not mentioned.
last_rejected.fix: Remove the parenthetical citation or verify if Sirach should be cited; the brief says only Gospels and Pauline epistles appear.
last_rejected.ruling: Source quotes Ἐλεημοσύναις...πίστεσιν; Sirach 3:30 is correct reference. Brief constraints don't override accurate scripture identification.

last_rejected.fix: For the Lord says / For he says
